Why, for a slotted packing pad
Best fatigue resistance and highest resilience of the eight, and the least creep under sustained load — so the gap it was fitted to hold stays held. Not for oil, and it perishes in prolonged sunlight
Where the pad is exposed to weather or sees oil. Good fatigue life with better ozone resistance than natural rubber
Low-cost enclosed packing. Fatigue life below natural rubber and no oil resistance
Weather, ozone and steam. Creeps more than natural rubber, so allow for it in the deflection
Where the pad sits in oil. Poor ozone resistance, so not for an exposed position
High temperature. Low tear strength makes it a weak choice for a slotted pad, where the slot is a stress raiser
Expensive sealing compounds with no fatigue advantage in a packing pad
Goes on without taking anything apart

The slot lets the pad slide in beside a bolt or shaft rather than over it. On a service job that is the difference between slackening a fastener and stripping an assembly — which is usually why the shape was chosen in the first place.
Hardness will not tell you how it behaves

Rubber bulges rather than compresses, so a thin wide pad is far stiffer than a thick narrow one of the same compound. Send the load and the gap you need held, and we set the shape and the hardness together.
It keeps sinking after you fit it
Rubber under permanent load creeps for years, and a packing pad that loses 2 mm has stopped doing its job. We allow for it at the design stage rather than shipping a pad that is correct on day one.
Tell us what holds it in

An open pad has one less thing keeping it in place than a closed one. Friction, a groove, adhesive or captive under the fastener — the answer changes the hardness and sometimes the outline, and it is the question that prevents a pad walking out under vibration.

What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes — but send the load as well as the pad. A pad taken out of service has crept and measures thinner than it was moulded, so copying its dimensions reproduces a part that is already part-worn. We work back from the gap it has to hold and what sits on it.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?

PDF, DWG and DXF. For this part a marked-up outline is enough — slot width to clear your fastener, overall size, and the thickness you need held. Add the load per pad and hardness becomes our output rather than your input.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412 and compression set to ASTM D395 Method B are tested in-house, and slot width is gauged against the fastener size on every batch.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?
TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Pads ship flat and unloaded.
